advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Persist the webhook-auth offset only after the metric is confirmed published (or publish before advancing the offset) so a failed put_metric_data does not permanently drop rejection deltas.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:230: `printf '%s\n' "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" >"$REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE"`
infra/scripts/observability.sh:238-240: `put_metric_data ... --metric-name reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections ... 2>/dev/null || true`
The offset write at line 230 precedes the put_metric_data at line 238; a failed/skipped publish advances the offset so those deltas never surface.
advisory.finding: The webhook-auth-rejection offset file is overwritten with the freshly-sampled counter value BEFORE put_metric_data runs, and put_metric_data swallows all errors (`2>/dev/null || true`). If publishing the metric fails, the offset has already advanced, so the un-published rejections are permanently lost from the alarm delta and the rotation failure can go un-paged.
scenarios: put_metric_data fails transiently (throttling, credential blip) during a probe window in which rejections occurred; the next window computes delta from the already-advanced offset and never re-publishes the missed rejections.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the webhook-auth-rejection metric is only trusted alongside reviewbot_healthy, or suppress/flag the metric when the health body is absent so an unreachable probe is not read as zero rejections.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:185: `review_webhook_auth_rejections=0`
infra/scripts/observability.sh:186: `if [ -n "$review_body" ]; then` — rejections are only parsed when a body exists; otherwise the default 0 is published as delta 0
The webhook-auth counter is derived solely from the health payload; an empty body yields the same published value (0) as a genuinely clean sample.
advisory.finding: When the review-bot health body is empty/unreachable, `review_webhook_auth_rejections` stays 0 and a delta of 0 is published to reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections — the auth-rejection metric cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'health probe returned no body'. The negative/absent result of the check is indistinguishable from the check never running for this metric.
scenarios: review-bot is down or /review/health times out with no body; the webhook-auth metric publishes 0 as if all deliveries were accepted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/enforce the nginx invariant that the public route always sets X-Forwarded-For (or rely primarily on the peer-address check), so the internal-webhook acceptance cannot be spoofed if nginx config drifts.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:233-234: docstring `Public nginx requests always carry ``X-Forwarded-For``, so absence of that header is the final guard`
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:246: `and not forwarded_for`

The guard's soundness rests on an nginx config invariant not enforced in this repo path; the peer-address check (client_host in resolved gerrit addresses) is the stronger gate but the XFF-absence assumption is load-bearing.
advisory.finding: Acceptance of the tokenless internal Gerrit path treats absence of X-Forwarded-For as the final guard against public-edge spoofing. This silently depends on nginx ALWAYS injecting X-Forwarded-For on the public route; if nginx config drifts (or a future route bypasses that header), a public client that can reach the peer and forge X-Origin-Url would be accepted. The coupling is undocumented in code beyond a docstring assertion.
scenarios: nginx proxy config is changed to not set X-Forwarded-For, or a new ingress path forwards to review-bot without it, allowing an attacker who can hit the peer to satisfy the internal path.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct ADR-0014 by a supersession/erratum annotation that preserves the original 'URL token secondary' decision text instead of rewriting the Decision and Consequences in place.
evidence: docs/adr/0014-inbound-webhook-auth.md:1 title changed to '... token public-only' and Status still 'Accepted' (line 3) while Decision #2 (lines 43-49) and #3 (lines 51-54) replace the prior URL-token decision

docs/documentation-policy.md:12 ADR correction method: 'Add substance-preserving annotations or errata, record supersession, or create a replacement ADR'; Exclusions include 'erased decision substance'

docs/adr/README.md via docs/adr/0042-auto-lander.md:3 and docs/adr/0090-main-fast-forward-only-submit.md:5 show the established method: a top annotation 'Superseded by ADR 00xx ... Kept for historical context; the decision below no longer reflects ...' that preserves the original decision text
advisory.finding: ADR-0014 (Status: Accepted) has its decision substance rewritten in place: the title, Context bullet ('any secret used must live in refs/meta/config'), Decision layer 2 ('SECONDARY — URL-embedded token'), Decision layer 3 (receiver-side token validation), the 'one and the same secret' statement, and the 'DEPENDENCY ON S5' consequence are all replaced with the new X-Origin-Url design, erasing the earlier accepted decision without a supersession or erratum annotation and while Status remains 'Accepted'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Restore the original ADR-0014 decision body and add a top-of-file supersession or erratum annotation (matching the ADR-0042 / ADR-0090 'Superseded by ... Kept for historical context' pattern) that records the new X-Origin-Url design, or create a replacement ADR and mark 0014 superseded.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct ADR-0010's changed rationale via a substance-preserving annotation/erratum rather than rewriting the accepted decision text in place.
evidence: docs/adr/0010-gerrit-github-replication.md:5 Status 'Accepted'; diff replaces the 'webhook URL token embedded in refs/meta/config' rationale and the ADR-0014 token dependency note with 'webhook routing policy' at lines ~44 and ~100
docs/documentation-policy.md:12 ADR correction method requires substance-preserving annotations/errata/supersession and excludes erased decision substance
docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md:71 shows the in-repo 'Superseded in part' annotation pattern that preserves the earlier text
advisory.finding: ADR-0010 (Status: Accepted) has its decision-supporting rationale rewritten in place: the specific 'webhook URL token embedded in refs/meta/config' statement and the 'inbound-webhook token's not-replicated-off-box property holds only while this stays false' dependency on ADR-0014 are replaced with 'webhook routing policy', modifying the recorded ADR rationale without a preserving annotation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Preserve the original ADR-0010 rationale text and add an erratum/annotation noting the ADR-0014 boundary change, following the 'Superseded in part' style used in docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Persist the webhook-auth offset file only after a successful put-metric-data, matching the replication_errors pattern (observability.sh:935-937).
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:230 `printf '%s\n' "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" >"$REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE" \`
Contrast the vetted pattern at infra/scripts/observability.sh:935-937: `if aws cloudwatch put-metric-data ... ; then echo "$total" > "$REPL_OFFSET_FILE"` — offset advanced only on publish success
put_metric_data at line 238-240 ends with `2>/dev/null || true`, so a publish failure is silent yet the offset is already advanced at line 230
infra/scripts/observability.sh:224-228 else-branch sets `review_webhook_auth_delta="$review_webhook_auth_rejections"` (full value, not 0)
infra/scripts/observability.sh:931-933 vetted rotation path: `[ "$new" -lt 0 ] && new=0` — publishes zero rather than double-counting when total < offset
advisory.finding: observability.sh writes the webhook-auth offset file UNCONDITIONALLY (line 230), unlike the established replication_errors pattern which only persists the offset AFTER a successful put-metric-data. If the CloudWatch publish at line 238-240 fails (the `|| true` swallows it), the offset is still advanced, so the rejections in that failed interval are permanently dropped and never counted toward the alarm.
merged_from: On a review-bot process restart (counter resets below the persisted offset), the delta logic publishes the FULL fresh counter value rather than 0. Since the process counter starts at 0 and only grows within the new process, this is usually the count since restart — but combined with the transient-probe reset above it can double-count. More importantly it diverges from the vetted rotation/reset handling which clamps to 0 to avoid double-counting retained/previously-published events.
scenarios: Transient AWS/CloudWatch API error during a probe interval that had real webhook-auth rejections
advisory.suggested_fix: Gate the offset write on publish success: only `printf ... > "$REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE"` inside the `if put_metric_data ...; then` branch, as replication_errors does.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not overwrite the webhook-auth offset when the health probe is unreachable/unparseable; skip the delta+persist step (as replication_errors leaves its offset untouched on an absent source).
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:185 `review_webhook_auth_rejections=0` (default when no body)
infra/scripts/observability.sh:195 `print("0 0")` on JSON parse failure → rejections sampled as 0
infra/scripts/observability.sh:230 unconditionally writes that 0 as the new offset

The vetted replication_errors handler at infra/scripts/observability.sh:940-944 deliberately does NOT overwrite the offset when its source is absent (it takes the else branch and leaves the offset untouched)
advisory.finding: When the review-bot health probe is unreachable/unparseable, review_webhook_auth_rejections is forced to 0 and that 0 is written to the offset file (line 230), resetting the baseline. On the next healthy probe the counter (e.g. 50) is >= prev(0), so the delta becomes the FULL counter value, republishing rejections that were already published in prior intervals — inflating the Sum-based alarm.
scenarios: review-bot briefly returns 503/empty body (restart, deploy) between two good probes
advisory.suggested_fix: Only run the delta computation and offset write when review_body was present and parsed (review_payload_ok computed); on an unreachable probe, publish nothing (or a 0 heartbeat) and leave the offset file unchanged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test: internal peer + no X-Forwarded-For + wrong/absent X-Origin-Url must return 401.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:243-248: `return ( bool(origin) and origin in expected_origins and not forwarded_for and client_host in _configured_gerrit_service_addresses(cfg) )`
test_gerrit_internal_webhook_does_not_need_unsupported_plugin_header varies only X-Forwarded-For (tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1844-1851)
test_gerrit_internal_webhook_requires_the_gerrit_service_peer varies only the resolved peer address (tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1875-1880)

Named violating input: a POST with resolved peer host, no X-Forwarded-For, and X-Origin-Url absent (or set to https://evil.example/) — the `bool(origin)`/`origin in expected_origins` branch — has no test asserting a 401.
advisory.finding: The new internal-Gerrit-origin auth path is not tested for a wrong/absent X-Origin-Url from a valid internal peer. `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` gates acceptance on `bool(origin) and origin in expected_origins`, but the two negative tests vary only the peer address and X-Forwarded-For — none drives a request from the resolved Gerrit service peer, with no X-Forwarded-For, carrying a wrong or missing X-Origin-Url, which must still be rejected.
scenarios: A caller reaching the internal peer address (or a co-tenant on the compose network) sends a request with a spoofed or empty X-Origin-Url; a regression loosening the origin check would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case in test_review_bot.py with `_resolve_host_addresses` returning `{"testclient"}`, no X-Forwarded-For, and either no X-Origin-Url or X-Origin-Url="https://evil.example/", asserting status_code == 401.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an observability test where a second window reports a higher rejection count than the first and assert the published value equals the increment (delta), not the raw counter.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:222-223: `if [ "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" -ge "$review_webhook_auth_prev" ]; then review_webhook_auth_delta=$(( review_webhook_auth_rejections - review_webhook_auth_prev ))`
test_reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections_publish_from_health_payload runs the script twice with the SAME health payload (rejections=3), asserting published values 3 then 0 — only the zero-delta case
test_reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections_survive_process_counter_reset exercises only the `rejections < prev` reset branch (offset=17, rejections=2 -> value 2)
Named violating input: two consecutive windows with rejections=3 then rejections=7 should publish delta 4; no test asserts this.
advisory.finding: The observability.sh per-window delta arithmetic for a genuine cross-window increase is untested. The intended metric is a per-interval delta (`rejections - prev`), but the only test that runs twice keeps rejections constant (3 then 3 -> delta 0), so the non-trivial increment case (e.g. prev=3, then rejections=7 -> delta 4) is never exercised; the counter-reset test only covers the `rejections < prev` branch.
scenarios: A regression in the subtraction (e.g. publishing the raw counter instead of the delta) would still pass, causing the CloudWatch Sum alarm to over- or under-count rejections across windows.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the publish test to run the script a second time with a health payload reporting rejections=7 (offset now 3) and assert `--value 4` is published.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm removing token auth on the internal webhook path (leaving only peer-IP + public X-Origin-Url) is an accepted authz relaxation, given the peer IP is the sole non-forgeable anchor and the token is no longer required.
evidence: `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` returns True on `bool(origin) and origin in expected_origins and not forwarded_for and client_host in _configured_gerrit_service_addresses(cfg)` — no secret is checked on this branch (app.py:243-248)

`origin = request.headers.get("X-Origin-Url", ...)` is a client-supplied header, and the expected value is the public canonical URL `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/` (config.py gerrit_canonical_web_url default; docker-compose.yml:145) — not a secret

`_webhook_authorized` falls through to `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` whenever the token compare fails (app.py:251-255), so the only remaining barrier for a tokenless request is the TCP peer IP resolving to the Gerrit service host
The prior design required the shared token on every webhook delivery; this change removes it for the internal path (diff: `header = X-Rebar-Token: __BOT_TOKEN__` deleted from webhooks.config)
`host = urlparse(cfg.gerrit_base_url).hostname; return _resolve_host_addresses(host)` returns the full getaddrinfo set (app.py:212-224)

`client_host in _configured_gerrit_service_addresses(cfg)` accepts membership in that resolved set (app.py:247) — the trust decision is entirely delegated to whatever the resolver returns at request time
On resolver failure `_resolve_host_addresses` returns an empty set (app.py:218-219), which fails closed for the internal path — but a broadened resolution fails open by widening the accepted peer set
advisory.finding: The internal Gerrit webhook path grants tokenless acceptance authenticated only by the non-secret client-controlled X-Origin-Url header plus the TCP peer IP; the cryptographic shared-secret (WEBHOOK_TOKEN) is no longer required for that path, so any process that presents the Gerrit service peer IP and the public canonical URL can inject arbitrary patchset-created/comment-added events and drive LLM-Review votes without any secret.
merged_from: _configured_gerrit_service_addresses resolves the Gerrit hostname per-request and accepts any client_host in that set; if the compose network ever resolves the Gerrit service name to multiple addresses (scaling/replicas) or another container transiently shares that IP, the tokenless internal branch would authorize non-Gerrit peers.
scenarios: A co-resident container on the shared compose bridge network that can source-spoof or acquire the Gerrit service IP posts to review-bot:8000/webhook with X-Origin-Url set to the public canonical URL and no X-Forwarded-For — accepted tokenlessly, enqueuing attacker-chosen change events.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 437 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 073f-b86f-42c6-456f has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 073f-b86f-42c6-456f` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 073f-b86f-42c6-456f` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 073f-b86f-42c6-456f --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
